paragraphs: We are a specialty finance company that invests in and finances residential mortgage assets. Our targeted investments include principally the following:

•Residential whole loans, including Non-QM loans, Business purpose loans, and Legacy RPL/NPL loans, which we acquire and hold through certain trusts that are consolidated on our balance sheet for financial reporting purposes. Through our wholly-owned subsidiary, Lima One Capital, LLC (together with its parent company, Lima One Holdings, LLC, "Lima One"), a leading nationwide originator and servicer of Business purpose loans (or BPLs), which we acquired on July 1, 2021, we originate and service BPLs for real estate investors. We also own real estate (or REO), which is typically acquired as a result of the foreclosure or other liquidation of delinquent whole loans in connection with our loan investment activities.
•Residential mortgage securities, including Agency MBS, Non-Agency MBS and CRT securities.

Our principal business objective is to deliver shareholder value through the generation of distributable income and through asset performance linked to residential mortgage credit fundamentals. We selectively invest in residential mortgage assets with a focus on credit analysis, projected prepayment rates, interest rate sensitivity and expected return. We are an internally-managed real estate investment trust (or REIT).

2025 delivered strong fixed income returns as markets benefited from a shift in monetary policy and continued macroeconomic resilience. Credit spreads tightened and the yield curve steepened over the year, with yields on two-year Treasuries declining by 78 basis points while ten-year Treasuries declined by 43 basis points. The Bloomberg US Aggregate Index returned 7.3% for the year, marking its strongest annual performance in five years. We capitalized on these constructive market conditions by accelerating the pace of capital deployment, benefiting from increased price stability and a favorable lending environment. While market conditions have improved and recession risks have moderated, we have maintained our emphasis on preserving sufficient liquidity, prudently managing our interest rate exposure, and using loan securitizations to minimize our exposure to margin risk.

We were incorporated in Maryland on July 24, 1997 and began operations on April 10, 1998. We have elected to be treated as a REIT for U.S. federal income tax purposes. In order to maintain our qualification as a REIT, we must comply with a number of requirements under federal tax law, including that we must distribute at least 90% of our annual REIT taxable income to our stockholders. We have elected to treat certain of our subsidiaries as taxable REIT subsidiaries (or TRS). In general, a TRS may hold assets and engage in activities that a REIT or qualified REIT subsidiary (or QRS) cannot hold or engage in directly, and a TRS may generally engage in any real estate or non-real estate related business.

We are a holding company and conduct our real estate finance businesses primarily through wholly-owned subsidiaries, so as to maintain an exemption from registration under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended (or the Investment Company Act) by ensuring that less than 40% of the value of our total assets, exclusive of U.S. Government securities and cash items (which we refer to as our adjusted total assets for Investment Company Act purposes), on an unconsolidated basis, consist of "investment securities" as defined by the Investment Company Act. We refer to this test as the "40% Test."

We primarily invest in and finance, through our various subsidiaries, residential mortgage assets. During 2025, we acquired approximately $2.7 billion of residential whole loans. This includes $0.9 billion of loans originated by our wholly-owned subsidiary, Lima One, which has funded more than $7.3 billion of loans since July 2021, when we fully acquired Lima One. At the end of 2025, residential whole loan investments comprised approximately 68% of our assets and 59% of our allocated net equity. During 2026, assuming economic conditions continue to support markets for residential mortgage assets, we expect to continue pursuing investment opportunities, focused primarily on residential whole loans and Agency MBS as market opportunities arise. We expect that our investment activities will continue to be financed primarily through a combination of securitization transactions, term loan warehouse financing and repurchase agreement financing.

At December 31, 2025, our total investment-related assets were comprised of the following: $8.8 billion, or approximately 71%, of residential whole loans (compared to $8.8 billion, or 83%, at December 31, 2024); $3.4 billion, or 27%, of residential mortgage securities (compared to $1.5 billion, or 14%, at December 31, 2024); and $301.2 million, or 2%, of remaining investment-related assets, comprised primarily of REO, capital contributions made to loan origination partners, other interest-earning assets, and loan-related receivables (compared to $299.5 million, or 3% at December 31, 2024).

During 2025, we continued to acquire or originate residential whole loans, with the majority of our additions being Non-QM loans. Our Residential whole loan portfolio includes primarily: (i) loans to finance (or refinance) one-to-four family residential properties that are not considered to meet the definition of a "Qualified Mortgage" in accordance with guidelines adopted by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ("Non-QM loans"), (ii) short-term business purpose loans collateralized by residential properties made to non-occupant borrowers that generally intend to rehabilitate or construct residential housing and then refinance or sell the properties ("Single-family transitional loans"); (iii) short-term business purpose loans collateralized by multifamily properties, typically with a loan balance below $10 million, made to non-occupant borrowers that generally intend to rehabilitate or stabilize and then refinance or sell the properties ("Multifamily transitional loans") (collectively, with Single-family transitional loans, "Transitional loans," also sometimes referred to as "Rehabilitation loans" or "Fix and Flip loans"), (iv) business purpose loans to finance (or refinance) non-owner occupied one-to-four family residential properties that are rented to one or more tenants ("Single-family rental loans" and, collectively with Transitional loans, "Business purpose loans"), and (v) loans primarily secured by residential real estate that were generally either non-performing or re-performing at acquisition ("Legacy RPL/NPL"). We acquire and hold our loans primarily through certain trusts that are consolidated on our balance sheet for financial reporting purposes.

Certain Legacy RPL/NPL loans acquired by the Company for which the Company did not elect the fair value option are accounted for as credit deteriorated, as they have experienced a deterioration in credit quality since origination and prior to our purchase and were acquired at discounted prices that reflect, in part, the impaired credit history of the borrower. Purchased Credit Deteriorated Loans are typically characterized by borrowers who had previously experienced payment delinquencies and the amount owed may have exceeded the value of the property pledged as collateral at the time of acquisition. The majority of these loans were also acquired at purchase prices that were discounted (often substantially so) to their contractual loan balance to reflect the impaired credit history of the borrower, the loan-to-value ratio (or LTV) of the loan and the coupon rate. Certain Legacy RPL/NPL acquired by the Company are accounted for as non-performing loans which are typically characterized by borrowers who have defaulted on their obligations and/or have payment delinquencies of 60 days or more at the time we acquire the loan. These loans were typically purchased at significantly discounted prices to the contractual loan balance.

We also own REO property as a result of managing the resolution of non-performing loans. The aggregate value of REO properties fluctuates based on the timing of resolutions of non-performing loans, valuation adjustments, and ultimate sales or disposal of properties.

We invest in residential mortgage securities, primarily Agency MBS, as well as Non-Agency MBS and CRT securities. During 2025, we opportunistically added $2.1 billion of Agency MBS. Going forward, we may continue to invest selectively in a range of residential mortgage securities as market opportunities arise.

Our financing strategy is designed to increase the size of our investment portfolio by borrowing against a substantial portion of the market value of the assets in our portfolio. For our Residential whole loan portfolio, we use loan securitizations, term warehouse facilities and shorter term repurchase agreements to finance our holdings of Residential whole loans. For our MBS portfolio, we primarily use shorter term repurchase agreements to finance our holdings of Securities. Going forward, in connection with our current and any future investment in residential whole loans, we expect that our financing strategy will continue to include loan securitization and other forms of structured financing, subject to market conditions.

The due diligence we undertake on potential investments may be limited and/or not reveal all of the risks associated with such investments and may not reveal other weaknesses in such assets, which could lead to losses.

The use of models in connection with the valuation and credit losses of our assets subjects us to potential risks in the event that such models are incorrect, misleading or based on incomplete information.
Mortgage loan modification and refinancing programs and future legislative action may materially adversely affect the value of, and the returns on, our MBS and residential whole loan investments.
Our investments in residential whole loans subject us to servicing-related risks, including those associated with foreclosure and liquidation.
Our ability to sell REO on terms acceptable to us or at all may be limited.
Our ownership of Lima One and investments in mortgage loan originators expose us to additional risks.
Business purpose loans involve a high degree of business and financial risk.

Prepayment rates on the mortgage loans underlying certain of our residential mortgage assets may materially adversely affect our profitability or could require us to sell assets in unfavorable market conditions.

However, the risks and uncertainties we face are not limited to those described below. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial may also adversely affect our business.

If any of the following risks and uncertainties develops into actual events or if the circumstances described in the risks and uncertainties occur or continue to occur, these events or circumstances could have a material adverse effect on our business, prospects, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows or liquidity. These events could also have a negative effect on the trading price of our securities.
•Economic developments and other factors that are out of our control may adversely affect our business operations.

•Our investments in residential mortgage loans (including BPLs), residential mortgage securities, commercial mortgage loans and other assets involve credit risk, which could materially adversely affect our results of operations.
•We may change our investment strategy, operating policies and/or asset allocations without stockholder consent, which could materially adversely affect our results of operations.
•Our investments are subject to changes in credit spreads and other risks.

paragraphs: The following discussion should be read in conjunction with our financial statements and accompanying notes included in Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

We are a specialty finance company that invests in and finances residential mortgage assets. We invest, on a leveraged basis, in residential whole loans, residential mortgage securities and other real estate assets. Through our wholly-owned subsidiary, Lima One, a leading nationwide originator and servicer of business purpose loans (or BPLs), we also originate and service business purpose loans for real estate investors. Our principal business objective is to deliver shareholder value through the generation of distributable income and through asset performance linked to residential mortgage credit fundamentals. We selectively invest in residential mortgage assets with a focus on credit analysis, projected prepayment rates, interest rate sensitivity and expected return. We are an internally-managed real estate investment trust.

At December 31, 2025, we had total assets of approximately $13.0 billion, of which $8.8 billion, or 68%, represented residential whole loans. Our residential whole loans include primarily: (i) loans to finance (or refinance) one-to-four family residential properties that are not considered to meet the definition of a "Qualified Mortgage" in accordance with guidelines adopted by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ("Non-QM loans"), (ii) business purpose loans primarily originated by Lima One, to finance (or refinance) non-owner occupied one-to-four family residential properties that are rented to one or more tenants ("Single-family rental loans"), (iii) short-term business purpose loans primarily originated by Lima One, collateralized by residential properties made to non-occupant borrowers that generally intend to rehabilitate or construct residential housing and then refinance or sell the properties ("Single-family transitional loans"), (iv) short-term business purpose loans primarily originated by Lima One, collateralized by multifamily properties, typically with a loan balance below $10 million, made to non-occupant borrowers that generally intend to rehabilitate or stabilize and then refinance or sell the properties ("Multifamily transitional loans, collectively with Single-family transitional loans, "Transitional loans," also sometimes referred to as "Rehabilitation loans" or "Fix and Flip loans" and, collectively with Single-family rental loans, "Business purpose loans"), (v) loans primarily secured by residential real estate that were generally either non-performing or re-performing at acquisition ("Legacy RPL/NPL") and (vi) loans on investor properties that conform to the standards for purchase by a federally chartered corporation, such as the Federal National Mortgage Association ("Fannie Mae") or the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation ("Freddie Mac") ("Agency eligible investor loans," which are included in "Other loans"). In addition, at December 31, 2025, we had approximately $3.3 billion or 25% of total assets invested in investments in Agency MBS.

The results of our business operations are affected by a number of factors, many of which are beyond our control, and primarily depend on, among other things, the level of our net interest income and the market value of our assets, liabilities and hedges that are accounted for at fair value through earnings, which is driven by numerous factors, including the supply and demand for residential mortgage assets in the marketplace, the terms and availability of adequate financing, general economic and real estate conditions (both on a national and local level), the impact of government actions in the real estate and mortgage sector, and the credit performance of our credit sensitive residential mortgage assets. Changes in these factors, or uncertainty in the market regarding the potential for changes in these factors, can result in significant changes in the value and/or performance of our investment portfolio. Further, our GAAP results may be impacted by market volatility, resulting in changes in market values of certain financial instruments for which changes in fair value are recorded in net income each period, including certain residential whole loans, securitized debt and Swaps. Our net interest income varies primarily as a result of changes in interest rates, the slope of the yield curve (i.e., the differential between long-term and short-term interest rates), borrowing costs (i.e., our interest expense), the level of loan delinquencies, which may result in changes in the amount of non-accrual loans, and prepayment speeds, the behavior of which involves various risks and uncertainties. Interest rates and conditional prepayment rates (or CPRs) (which is an annualized measure of the amount of unscheduled principal prepayments on an asset as a percentage of the asset balance), vary according to the type of investment, conditions in the financial markets, competition and other factors, none of which can be predicted with any certainty. Our financial results are also impacted by estimates of credit losses that are required to be recorded when loans that are not accounted for at fair value through net income are acquired or originated, as well as changes in these credit loss estimates that will be required to be made periodically.

With respect to our business operations, increases in interest rates, in general, may, over time, cause: (i) the interest expense associated with our borrowings to increase; (ii) the value of certain of our residential mortgage assets and securitized debt to decline; (iii) coupons on our adjustable-rate assets to reset, on a delayed basis, to higher interest rates; (iv) prepayments on our assets to decline, thereby slowing the amortization of purchase premiums and the accretion of our purchase discounts, and slowing our ability to redeploy capital to generally higher yielding investments; and (v) the value of our derivative hedging instruments, if any, to increase. Conversely, decreases in interest rates, in general, may, over time, cause: (i) the interest expense associated with our borrowings to decrease; (ii) the value of certain of our residential mortgage assets and securitized debt, to increase; (iii) coupons on

our adjustable-rate assets, on a delayed basis, to lower interest rates; (iv) prepayments on our assets to increase, thereby accelerating the amortization of purchase premiums and the accretion of our purchase discounts, and accelerating the redeployment of our capital to generally lower yielding investments; and (v) the value of our derivative hedging instruments, if any, to decrease. Further, changes in spreads will also impact the valuation of our residential mortgage assets and securitized debt, which could result in volatility in GAAP earnings. In addition, our borrowing costs and credit lines are further affected by the type of collateral we pledge and general conditions in the credit market.

Our investments in residential mortgage assets expose us to credit risk, meaning that we are generally subject to credit losses due to the risk of delinquency, default and foreclosure on the underlying real estate collateral. Our investment process for credit sensitive assets focuses primarily on quantifying and pricing credit risk. With respect to investments in Business purpose and Non-QM loans, we believe that sound underwriting standards, including low LTVs at origination, significantly mitigate our risk of loss. Further, we believe the discounted purchase prices paid on Legacy RPL/NPL loans mitigate our risk of loss in the event that we receive less than 100% of the unpaid principal balance of these investments.

Premiums arise when we acquire an MBS at a price in excess of the aggregate principal balance of the mortgages securing the MBS (i.e., par value) or when we acquire residential whole loans at a price in excess of their unpaid principal balance. Conversely, discounts arise when we acquire an MBS at a price below the aggregate principal balance of the mortgages securing the MBS or when we acquire residential whole loans at a price below their unpaid principal balance. Accretable purchase discounts on these investments are accreted to interest income. Premiums paid to purchase loans are amortized against interest income over the life of the investment using the effective yield method, adjusted for actual prepayment activity. An increase in the prepayment rate, as measured by the CPR, will typically accelerate the amortization of purchase premiums, thereby reducing the interest income earned on these assets.

CPR levels are impacted by, among other things, conditions in the housing market, new regulations, government and private sector initiatives, interest rates, availability of credit to home borrowers, underwriting standards and the economy in general. In particular, CPR presents the annualized constant rate of principal repayment in excess of scheduled principal amortization. CPRs on our residential mortgage securities and whole loans may differ significantly. For the year ended December 31, 2025, the average CPRs on certain of our loan portfolios were: 14.3% for Non-QM loans, 10.5% for Single-family rental loans, and 8.1% for Legacy RPL/NPL loans. In addition, for the year ended December 31, 2025, the repayment rate (which includes both scheduled and unscheduled repayments of principal) was 67.7% for our Single-family transitional loans and 42.5% for our Multifamily transitional loans.

It is generally our business strategy to hold our residential mortgage assets as long-term investments. As part of Lima One's mortgage banking activities, from time to time, we sell certain loans shortly after origination. On at least a quarterly basis, excluding investments for which the fair value option has been elected or for which specialized loan accounting is otherwise applied, we assess our ability and intent to continue to hold each asset and, as part of this process, we monitor our investments in securities that are designated as AFS for impairment. A change in our ability and/or intent to continue to hold any of these securities that are in an unrealized loss position, or a deterioration in the underlying characteristics of these securities, could result in our recognizing future impairment charges or a loss upon the sale of any such security.

Our residential mortgage investments have longer-term contractual maturities than our non-securitization related financing liabilities, and the interest rates we pay on our non-securitization related financings will typically change at a faster pace than the interest rates we earn on our investments. In order to reduce this interest rate risk exposure, we may enter into derivative instruments, which currently include Swaps.

Following years of volatility, 2025 delivered strong fixed income returns as markets benefited from a shift in monetary policy and continued macroeconomic resilience. Credit spreads tightened and the yield curve steepened over the year, with yields on two-year Treasuries declining by 78 basis points while ten-year Treasuries declined by 43 basis points. The Bloomberg US Aggregate Index returned 7.3% for the year, marking its strongest annual performance in five years. We capitalized on these constructive market conditions by accelerating the pace of capital deployment, benefiting from increased price stability and a favorable lending environment. During 2025, we were able to add $4.8 billion of our target assets at attractive yields. These additions included $2.1 billion of Agency MBS, $1.8 billion of Non-QM loans, and approximately $900 million of funded originations of Business purpose loans and draws on existing Transitional loans at Lima One. During 2025, we executed five securitizations and issued $1.7 billion of securitized debt.

During the year, we generated GAAP earnings per share (or EPS) of $1.31 per basic common share and Distributable earnings, a non-GAAP financial measure that excludes the impact of fair value changes and certain other items, of $1.00 per basic common share. For the year, compensation and benefits and other G&A expenses were $119.4 million, a 9.5% reduction from $131.9 million incurred in 2024 attributable to expense reduction initiatives. At December 31, 2025, our GAAP book value was $13.20 and our Economic book value, a non-GAAP financial measure of our financial position that adjusts GAAP book value by the amount of unrealized mark-to-market gains or losses on our residential whole loans and securitized debt held at carrying value, was $13.75 per common share, each down approximately 1% compared to December 31, 2024. During the year, we declared dividends totaling $1.44 per common share.

For the year, our Lima One subsidiary originated Business purpose loans with a maximum unpaid principal balance of $0.9 billion, a decrease from the $1.4 billion originated in 2024. During the year, we expanded Lima One's sales force, invested in technology initiatives that we expect to improve the borrower experience, and made key hires to Lima One's leadership team in strategic growth areas. In early 2026, we relaunched multifamily lending and began funding loans through our newly established wholesale channel, which represent two key areas of growth for Lima One. During 2025, Lima One sold $212.9 million of recently originated single-family rental loans to third parties and realized gains of $6.1 million. We believe that these sales to third parties help to strengthen Lima One's franchise value, create additional distribution channels to accommodate future growth, and enhance returns.
本公司為一家專業財務公司，投資並融資住宅房貸資產。我們的目標投資主要包括以下項目：

•住宅整貸，包括非QM貸款、商業用途貸款及遺留RPL/NPL貸款，我們透過特定信託取得並持有，這些信託已納入我們的資產負債表以進行財務報導。透過我們的 wholly-owned 子公司 Lima One Capital, LLC（與其母公司 Lima One Holdings, LLC 合稱為 "Lima One"），一家全國性的商業用途貸款（或BPLs）發行與服務機構，我們於2021年7月1日取得該公司，我們為不動產投資者發行並服務BPLs。我們也擁有不動產（或REO），通常是因房貸投資活動中違約貸款的拍賣或其它清算程序而取得。
•住宅房貸證券，包括機構MBS、非機構MBS及CRT證券。
我們的主要業務目標是透過產生可分配收入及與住宅房貸信貸基本面相關的資產表現，來為股東創造價值。我們選擇性投資於住宅房貸資產，重點在於信用分析、預期提前償還率、利率敏感度及預期回報。本公司為一 internally-managed 不動產投資信託（或REIT）。

2025年固定收益表現強勁，市場受益於貨幣政策的轉變及總體經濟韌性持續。信用利差收窄，收益率曲線走陡，全年兩年期國庫券收益率下降78個基點，十年期國庫券收益率下降43個基點。彭博美國總體債券指數全年回報率為7.3%，為近五年來最佳年度表現。我們利用這些有利市場條件，加快資本部署速度，受益於價格穩定性提升及有利的貸款環境。雖然市場條件改善，經濟衰退風險已降低，我們仍維持對保持足夠流動性、謹慎管理利率風險敞口及透過貸款證券化來降低邊際風險敞口的重視。

本公司於1997年7月24日在馬裏蘭州註冊成立，並於1998年4月10日開始營運。我們已選擇以REIT方式納入美國聯邦所得稅目的。為維持REIT資格，我們必須遵守聯邦稅法下的若干要求，包括我們必須將至少90%的年度REIT應稅所得分配給股東。我們已選擇將部分子公司視為應稅REIT子公司（或TRS）。一般而言，TRS可持有資產並從事REIT或合格REIT子公司（或QRS）不能直接持有的資產或從事的活動，TRS可從事任何不動產或非不動產相關業務。
本公司為一家控股公司，主要透過 wholly-owned 子公司進行不動產融資業務，以維持免於根據1940年投資公司法（或投資公司法）進行註冊的豁免，確保我們的總資產價值（扣除美國政府證券及現金項目，我們稱為投資公司法目的的調整總資產）中，不包括投資證券的價值在未合併基礎上少於40%。我們稱此為 "40%測試"。

於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司之總投資相關資產包含以下項目：8.8 十億美元，或約 71%，為住宅整貸 (與 2024 年 12 月 31 日之 8.8 十億美元，或 83%，比較)；3.4 十億美元，或 27%，為住宅房貸證券 (與 2024 年 12 月 31 日之 1.5 十億美元，或 14%，比較)；以及 301.2 百萬美元，或 2%，為其餘投資相關資產，主要包含 REO、對貸款發行夥伴之資本投資、其他產生利息之資產，以及貸款相關應收款 (與 2024 年 12 月 31 日之 299.5 百萬美元，或 3%，比較)。

於 2025 年，我們持續取得或發放住宅整貸，其中絕大多數新增貸款為非 QM 貸款。我們的住宅整貸組合主要包括：(i) 用以資助（或重新貸款）一至四戶住宅不動產的貸款，且這些貸款不被視為符合消費者金融保護局（"Consumer Financial Protection Bureau"）所採用的「合格房貸」（"Qualified Mortgage"）定義（"非 QM 貸款"），(ii) 短期用於商業用途的貸款，以住宅不動產為擔保，貸款人為非實際佔有者，通常意圖進行住宅不動產的修復或建設，並之後重新貸款或出售該不動產（"單戶過渡貸款"）；(iii) 短期用於商業用途的貸款，以多戶住宅不動產為擔保，貸款餘額通常低於 10 百萬美元，貸款人為非實際佔有者，通常意圖進行住宅不動產的修復或穩定，並之後重新貸款或出售該不動產（"多戶過渡貸款"）（合稱為 "過渡貸款"，有時也稱為 "修復貸款" 或 "翻修貸款"），(iv) 用以資助（或重新貸款）非所有權人佔有的住宅不動產貸款，該不動產出租給一個或多個租客（"單戶出租貸款"，與過渡貸款合稱為 "商業用途貸款"），以及 (v) 以住宅不動產為擔保的貸款，通常在取得時為非 performing 或 re-performing（"Legacy RPL/NPL"）。我們主要透過某些信託取得並持有這些貸款，這些信託在財務報導目的上被合併至我們的資產負債表中。

本公司取得之某些遺留 RPL/NPL 貸款，若本公司未選擇公平價值選項，則以其信用品質惡化為基礎進行會計處理，因其自發行以來至本公司取得前已出現信用品質惡化，且取得價格反映借款人信用歷史部分之減損。所購信用品質惡化貸款通常為借款人先前曾有逾期付款紀錄，且於取得時所欠金額可能高於擔保不動產之價值。這些貸款大多數亦以顯著折扣（有時大幅折扣）取得，以反映借款人信用歷史、貸款價值比（或 LTV）及票面利率。本公司取得之某些遺留 RPL/NPL 亦以非表現貸款為基礎進行會計處理，通常為借款人於本公司取得貸款時已違約或逾期付款達 60 天以上。這些貸款通常以顯著折扣取得，以反映其合同貸款餘額。
本公司亦因管理非表現貸款之解決過程而擁有 REO 不動產。REO 不動產總價值會因非表現貸款解決時間、評估調整及最終出售或處置不動產而有所變動。
本公司投資於住宅房貸證券，主要包括機構 MBS，以及非機構 MBS 及 CRT 證券。於 2025 年，本公司機會性增加 21 億美元機構 MBS。未來，本公司可能根據市場機會，持續選擇性投資於住宅房貸證券。
本公司之融資策略旨在透過對投資組閤中資產市場價值之大部份進行貸款，以增加投資組合規模。針對本公司之住宅整貸組合，本公司使用貸款證券化、定期倉儲融資及短期買回協議以融資住宅整貸之持有。針對本公司之 MBS 組合，本公司主要使用短期買回協議以融資證券之持有。未來，就本公司目前及任何未來對住宅整貸之投資，本公司預期融資策略將持續包含貸款證券化及其他形式之結構化融資，並視市場條件而定。

paragraphs: 以下討論應配合我們的財務報表及附註說明，請參閱本年度10-K申報表第8項所載內容。

本公司為專業財務公司，投資並提供住宅房貸資產之融資。我們以槓桿方式投資住宅整貸、住宅房貸證券及其他不動產資產。透過我們百分之百擁有之子公司Lima One，為全國首屈一指之商業用途貸款（或BPLs）發行與服務機構，我們亦為不動產投資者發行與服務商業用途貸款。本公司主要業務目標為透過產生可分配收入及與住宅房貸信用基本面相關之資產表現，來為股東創造價值。我們選擇性投資住宅房貸資產，重點在於信用分析、預期提前償還率、利率敏感度及預期回報。本公司為內部管理之不動產投資信託。

截至2025年12月31日，本公司總資產約為13.0十億美元，其中8.8十億美元，或68%，為住宅整貸。本公司之住宅整貸主要包括：(i) 用以資金融資（或重貸）非屬「合格房貸」（Qualified Mortgage）定義之單戶至四戶住宅不動產貸款（依消費者金融保護局所訂標準）（Non-QM貸款），(ii) 由Lima One主要發行之商業用途貸款，用以資金融資（或重貸）非自用之單戶至四戶住宅不動產，出租予一個或多個租客（Single-family rental loans），(iii) 短期商業用途貸款，主要由Lima One發行，以住宅不動產為擔保，貸款予非佔用借款人，通常意圖進行住宅不動產之修復或興建，並後續重貸或出售（Single-family transitional loans），(iv) 短期商業用途貸款，主要由Lima One發行，以多戶住宅不動產為擔保，貸款餘額通常低於10百萬美元，貸款予非佔用借款人，通常意圖進行住宅不動產之修復或穩定，並後續重貸或出售（Multifamily transitional loans，與Single-family transitional loans合稱為Transitional loans，亦有時稱為Rehabilitation loans或Fix and Flip loans，與Single-family rental loans合稱為Business purpose loans），(v) 以住宅不動產為擔保之貸款，通常在取得時為非表現或重新表現貸款（Legacy RPL/NPL），(vi) 符合由聯邦特許機構（如美國聯邦住宅貸款銀行管理局（Fannie Mae）或美國聯邦住房貸款銀行（Freddie Mac）所訂購標準之投資不動產貸款（Agency eligible investor loans），包含於Other loans中。此外，截至2025年12月31日，本公司約有3.3十億美元或總資產25%投資於Agency MBS。

本公司營運成果受多項因素影響，許多因素為本公司所無法控制，且主要取決於諸多因素，包括本公司淨利息收入水準及資產、負債與對沖之市場價值（以收益計入），而此等價值受多項因素影響，包括住宅房貸資產之市場供需、貸款之條件與充足融資之可得性、總體經濟與不動產條件（國家與地方層面），政府於不動產與房貸產業之行動影響，以及本公司信用敏感性住宅房貸資產之信用表現。這些因素之變動，或市場對這些因素變動潛力之不確定性，可能導致本公司投資組合之價值與/或表現產生重大變動。此外，本公司之GAAP結果可能受市場波動影響，導致某些金融工具之市場價值變動，而此等變動會在每個會計期間計入淨收入，包括某些住宅整貸、證券化債務與Swaps。本公司之淨利息收入主要因利率變動、收益率曲線傾斜度（即長期與短期利率之差異）、借款成本（即本公司之利息支出）、貸款違約率水準，可能導致非應計貸款之金額變動，以及提前償還速度，其行為涉及多種風險與不確定性。利率與條件性提前償還率（或CPRs）（為資產之未預期本金償還額佔資產餘額之年度化衡量指標）會根據投資類型、金融市場條件、競爭情形及其他因素而有所不同，而這些因素均無法預測。本公司之財務結果亦受貸款信用損失之估計影響，此等估計在取得或發行非以收益計入之貸款時必須記錄，且需定期重新評估此等信用損失估計。

就我們的業務運作而言，利率的上升，一般而言，可能隨時間推移導致：(i) 我們借款所產生的利息支出增加；(ii) 某些我們的住宅抵押貸款資產與證券化債務的價值下降；(iii) 我們可調利率資產的票息，延遲重設為較高的利率；(iv) 我們資產的提前償還減少，因而減緩購買 premiums 的攤銷與購買折扣的累計，並減緩我們重新配置資本至一般較高收益率投資的能力；以及 (v) 我們的衍生性避險工具，如有，價值上升。相反地，利率的下降，一般而言，可能隨時間推移導致：(i) 我們借款所產生的利息支出減少；(ii) 某些我們的住宅抵押貸款資產與證券化債務的價值上升；(iii) 我們可調利率資產的票息，延遲重設為較低的利率；(iv) 我們資產的提前償還增加，因而加速購買 premiums 的攤銷與購買折扣的累計，並加速我們重新配置資本至一般較低收益率投資的能力；以及 (v) 我們的衍生性避險工具，如有，價值下降。此外，利差的變化也會影響我們住宅抵押貸款資產與證券化債務的評價，這可能會導致 GAAP 盈餘的波動。此外，我們的借款成本與信用線也受到我們提供的擔保品類型與信用市場整體情況的影響。

我們在住宅抵押貸款資產上的投資使我們面臨信用風險，意味著我們一般會因基礎實物資產抵押品的違約、違約與法拍風險而遭受信用損失。我們對信用敏感性資產的投資流程主要著重於量化與評價信用風險。就投資於商業用途與非 QM 貸款而言，我們認為健全的授信標準，包括貸款發放時的低 LTV，顯著降低我們的損失風險。此外，我們認為對 Legacy RPL/NPL 貸款支付的折扣購入價格，也降低我們在這些投資中，若無法收到 100% 未償還本金的情況下，所面臨的損失風險。

當我們以高於抵押貸款總本金金額的價格取得 MBS 時，就會產生 premiums（即溢價）；或當我們以高於住宅整貸未償還本金金額的價格取得住宅整貸時，也會產生 premiums。相反地，當我們以低於抵押貸款總本金金額的價格取得 MBS 時，就會產生 discounts（即折價）；或當我們以低於住宅整貸未償還本金金額的價格取得住宅整貸時，也會產生 discounts。這些投資的可攤銷購買折扣會計入利息收入。為取得貸款所支付的 premiums 會根據實際提前償還情況，使用有效收益率法，在投資的整個存續期間內攤銷至利息收入。提前償還率（以 CPR 測量）的增加，通常會加速購買 premiums 的攤銷，從而減少這些資產所產生的利息收入。

Premiums 是指我們以高於抵押貸款總本金金額的價格取得 MBS 時所產生的差額（即 par value）；或以高於住宅整貸未償還本金金額的價格取得住宅整貸時所產生的差額。相反地，discounts 是指我們以低於抵押貸款總本金金額的價格取得 MBS 時所產生的差額；或以低於住宅整貸未償還本金金額的價格取得住宅整貸時所產生的差額。這些投資的可攤銷購買折扣會計入利息收入。為取得貸款所支付的 premiums 會根據實際提前償還情況，使用有效收益率法，在投資的整個存續期間內攤銷至利息收入。

CPR 水準受多種因素影響，包括但不限於房地產市場的情況、新法規、政府與民間部門的措施、利率、對購屋貸款者的信貸可得性、貸款審核標準以及總體經濟。特別而言，CPR 顯示的是每年固定本金償還率超過預定本金減免的年化常數率。我們的住宅抵押貸款證券與整筆貸款的 CPR 可能有顯著差異。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們某些貸款組合的平均 CPR 為：非 QM 貸款為 14.3%、單戶出租貸款為 10.5%、以及遺留 RPL/NPL 貸款為 8.1%。此外，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的單戶過渡貸款的償還率（包含預定與非預定本金償還）為 67.7%，而我們的多戶過渡貸款為 42.5%。

我們的業務策略通常是將住宅抵押貸款資產作為長期投資。作為 Lima One 的房貸銀行業務之一部分，我們有時會在貸款發行後不久出售部分貸款。除已選用公允價值選項或已應用特殊貸款會計的投資外，我們至少每季評估我們持續持有每一項資產的能力與意圖，並在這個過程中監測被指定為 AFS 的投資是否發生減值。若我們持續持有這些投資的意圖或能力發生變化，或這些投資的基礎特性惡化，可能會導致我們認列未來減值費用或在出售這些投資時產生損失。
我們的住宅抵押貸款投資的長期契約到期日長於我們非證券化相關的融資負債，且我們在非證券化相關融資上支付的利率通常會比我們在投資上獲得的利率變動得更快。為降低這種利率風險，我們可能會進行衍生工具交易，目前包括掉期合約。

經歷多年的波動後，2025 年固定收益市場表現強勁，受益於貨幣政策的轉變與總體經濟的持續韌性。信用利差收窄，收益率曲線變陡，全年兩年期國庫券收益率下降 78 基點，十年期國庫券收益率下降 43 基點。彭博美國總體債券指數在該年回報 7.3%，為過去五年最佳年度表現。我們把握這些有利市場條件，加快資本部署的速度，受益於價格穩定與有利的貸款環境。2025 年，我們成功增加 4.8 十億美元的目標資產，這些資產包括 2.1 十億美元的機構 MBS、1.8 十億美元的非 QM 貸款，以及約 9 億美元的商業用途貸款資金發行與現有過渡貸款的提款。2025 年，我們進行了五次證券化交易，並發行了 1.7 十億美元的證券化債務。

本年，我們產生了 1.31 美元的 GAAP 每股盈餘（或 EPS），以及 Distributable 盈餘，這是一項非 GAAP 財務指標，排除了公允價值變動及其他某些項目影響的 1.00 美元每股盈餘。本年，薪資與福利及其他 G&A 費用為 119.4 百萬美元，較 2024 年的 131.9 百萬美元減少 9.5%，這是因費用削減措施所致。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的 GAAP 書面價值為 13.20 美元，而 Economic 書面價值，這是一項非 GAAP 財務指標，調整 GAAP 書面價值以反映我們住宅整筆貸款與證券化債務的未實現市價盈虧，為 13.75 美元每股，與 2024 年 12 月 31 日相比，均下降約 1%。本年，我們宣佈了 1.44 美元每股的股息。

本年，我們的 Lima One 子公司發放了總計最高未償還本金餘額為 0.9 十億美元的商業用途貸款，較 2024 年發放的 1.4 十億美元減少。在本年期間，我們擴充了 Lima One 的銷售團隊，投資於科技計畫，預期將改善借款人體驗，並在戰略成長領域聘請了 Lima One 領導團隊的重要人選。2026 年初，我們重新推出多單位住宅貸款業務，並透過新設立的 wholesale 頻道開始資助貸款，這兩者為 Lima One 的兩大成長領域。2025 年，Lima One 將最近發放的單戶出租貸款總計 212.9 百萬美元出售給第三方，並實現獲利 6.1 百萬美元。我們認為這些出售給第三方的交易有助於強化 Lima One 的品牌價值，建立額外的分銷通路以因應未來成長，並提高回報。

paragraphs: 本節說明可能影響本公司及其業務的特定風險。讀者應謹慎考量下列各項風險，以及本年度報告表10-K中所載的其他資訊。根據本公司目前所知的資訊，我們認為下列資訊識別出對本公司最重要的風險因素。然而，我們所面臨的風險與不確定性並不限於下列所描述的內容。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前本公司尚未知悉，或目前認為不重要，也可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。
若下列風險與不確定性發展為實際事件，或所描述的情況發生或持續發生，這些事件或情況可能對本公司業務、前景、財務狀況、營運成果、現金流或流動性產生重大不利影響。這些事件也可能對本公司證券的交易價格產生負面影響。
